items.prompt: If an attacker gets administrator access in production, can the attacker delete our backups?
items.ten_second: Not if the backup vault is locked in compliance mode, with a copy in another account. Governance mode does not stop an administrator.
sixty_second: The short answer is: not if the backup vault is locked in compliance mode.
It works like this. AWS Backup Vault Lock protects the backups in a vault.
If anyone tries to delete a backup or change its lifecycle, AWS Backup denies it.
That includes the root user.
Compliance mode starts with a grace time of at least three days.
During that time, you can still remove the lock. After it, no user can change it.
The thing to watch is governance mode.
A user with enough IAM permissions can remove that lock. So can an attacker with administrator access.
Also copy your backups to a second account in your organization.
If a backup is deleted, you copy it back and restore it.
In your case, I'd put the locked vault in a separate backup account.
Who can sign in to that account today?
skeleton: compliance lock denies deletes, even root

key_points.point: If any user, including the root user, tries to delete a backup or change its lifecycle in a locked vault, AWS Backup denies the operation.
accept: even the root user cannot delete a locked backup
the lock blocks deletes and lifecycle changes

key_points.point: After the grace time, a compliance-mode lock cannot be altered or deleted by any user.
accept: after the grace time nobody can remove a compliance lock
compliance mode becomes permanent

key_points.point: A governance-mode lock can be removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions.
accept: an administrator can remove a governance lock
governance mode does not stop admins

key_points.point: With a cross-account copy in your organization, you can copy a deleted original backup back from the destination account and then restore it.
accept: keep a copy in a second account
copy the backup back and restore it

key_points.point: The grace time of a compliance-mode lock is at least 3 days (72 hours), and during it you can still remove the lock.
accept: you can test the lock for a few days first
the lock can be removed during the grace time

key_points.point: Vault access policies only control user access to AWS Backup APIs; EBS and RDS snapshots also need separate access policies in IAM.
accept: the vault policy covers only the AWS Backup APIs
also limit the EBS and RDS snapshot APIs in IAM

must_not_say.error: Vault Lock means nobody can ever delete a backup.
must_not_say.correct: That depends on the mode. A governance-mode lock can be removed by users with sufficient IAM permissions.

must_not_say.error: Locked backups stay even if we close the account.
must_not_say.correct: If you close the account and do not reopen it in time, AWS deletes the contents of the backup vault, even if AWS Backup Vault Lock was in place.

follow_ups.question: Can we test the lock before it becomes permanent?
follow_ups.answer: Yes. In compliance mode the grace time is at least 3 days (72 hours). During the grace time you can still remove the vault lock and change its configuration.

follow_ups.question: What happens if we set the retention too long?
follow_ups.answer: Backups in a locked vault cannot be deleted until their lifecycle completes, so they keep costing storage. A recovery point with retention set to Always is retained forever after the grace time.

items.prompt: We already have RDS automated backups and EBS snapshots. Why would we add AWS Backup?
items.persona: a startup founder in office hours
items.ten_second: Both give you backups. AWS Backup adds one policy across services and accounts, a lock, and audit reports. Your native backups keep working.
sixty_second: Both give you backups, and your RDS and EBS settings keep working as before.
The difference is control from one place, across services and accounts.
It works like this. AWS Backup manages and monitors backups across your services from a single place.
One backup plan picks resources by tag, with a schedule and a retention period.
Vault Lock helps prevent manual deletion of those backups.
And Audit Manager reports on whether your backups follow the policy.
The thing to watch is that AWS Backup doesn't govern backups made outside it.
So the automated backups that RDS makes on its own stay outside that policy.
In your case, I'd start with one plan for the production databases and volumes.
How many accounts hold data that you must keep?

key_points.point: AWS Backup manages and monitors backups across the AWS services you use, including EBS volumes, from a single place.
accept: one place for all backups
it manages backups across services

key_points.point: All existing per-service backup capabilities remain unchanged when you use AWS Backup.
accept: RDS and EBS backups keep working
it does not replace the native backups

key_points.point: Backups that other AWS services create on their own are not available for central governance through AWS Backup.
accept: native backups are not governed by AWS Backup
backups made outside AWS Backup are not in its policy

key_points.point: AWS Backup Vault Lock helps prevent manual deletion of backups and checks that backups are stored with a Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) model.
accept: a lock stops manual deletes
write once, read many

key_points.point: AWS Backup Audit Manager audits and reports on the compliance of your data protection policies.
accept: audit reports for the backup policy
proof for auditors

key_points.point: How AWS Backup relates to native backups varies by service: for RDS continuous backups it uses the same infrastructure, for DynamoDB it is a separate backup layer.
accept: for some services it uses the same backups
for DynamoDB it is a separate layer

must_not_say.error: AWS Backup replaces RDS automated backups.
must_not_say.correct: All existing per-service backup capabilities remain unchanged when you use AWS Backup.

must_not_say.error: AWS Backup also governs the snapshots our scripts make.
must_not_say.correct: AWS Backup does not govern backups you take in your AWS environment outside of AWS Backup.

follow_ups.question: What do we pay for?
follow_ups.answer: You pay for the backup storage you use, backup data transferred between Regions, backup data you restore, and backup evaluations. There is no minimum fee and no setup charge.

follow_ups.question: Can it also back up our servers on premises?
follow_ups.answer: Yes. AWS Backup can back up on-premises Storage Gateway volumes and VMware virtual machines, so you manage backups both on premises and on AWS in one way.
